findings.title: The hero card shows only tides, while the copy promises gate times, depth and notices

location.description: the card "Today at Porthmellin" beside the headline

findings.viewer_experience: A harbor master judging "can stand behind" sees only a tide table, which any almanac gives.

current.value: four tide rows only: no gate times, no depth, no notice

findings.target: the card shows gate times, a depth reading and one notice as well as the tides, so it looks like the page berth holders open; on the tablet the card shows the same content
findings.fix_direction: Add gate times, a depth reading and one notice to the card. The example values for these must come from the maker; do not invent them.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees gate times, a depth reading and a notice in the card, in the desktop, tablet and widescreen viewports.

findings.title: The three notes are 181 px columns on the tablet, about 20 to 23 characters per line

location.description: the three notes "Lock gate times", "Depth at the pontoon" and "Notices" at 768 px

findings.viewer_experience: The eye jumps back every three or four words, and the rags are uneven.
findings.target: 45 to 75 characters per line, using the phone's one-column stack or two columns at this width
findings.fix_direction: Use the phone's one-column stack, or two columns, at 768 px.
findings.source: Bringhurst, 45 to 75 characters for a line

closed_when.check: characters_per_line of section.points > div.point > p in the tablet viewport is 30 or more

findings.title: The copy does not say what the card is, or how Tidewell differs from the office's current method

location.description: the hero paragraph and the table title

findings.viewer_experience: A stranger cannot tell whether Porthmellin is a customer, a demo or their own harbor, and nothing sets Tidewell against a chalkboard, a printed table or phone calls.

current.value: copy unchanged; no label, no comparison, no source for the tide predictions

findings.target: the card is labeled as the page berth holders see, one line sets Tidewell against the office's current method, and the source of the tide predictions is named
findings.fix_direction: Label the card as the page berth holders see and add one line against the office's current method. The source of the tide predictions is a fact only the maker has; the maker must supply it.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees, in all four viewports, a label on the card as the page berth holders see, a line against the current method, and a named source for the tide predictions.

findings.title: On the tablet the table card stops at x 624 while the nav and notes run to x 704

location.description: the table card under the hero on the tablet

findings.viewer_experience: The card's right edge is off the column the nav and notes use.

current.value: card right edge at x 624; nav and notes at x 704

findings.target: the card is the full content width, right edge at x 704
findings.fix_direction: Make the card the full content width.

closed_when.check: A fresh critic sees the card's right edge line up with the nav and the notes in the tablet viewport.

findings.title: On the tablet the hero paragraph runs at 77 characters per line, just over 75

location.description: the hero paragraph on the tablet

findings.viewer_experience: The line is a little longer than comfortable.

closed_when.check: characters_per_line of div.hero-text > p in the tablet viewport is 75 or fewer
